rationale: The denominator's |cumulative accrual| term is tiny relative to total assets for most firms, so the signal collapses to a 3-year R&D-to-assets ratio — the well-documented R&D-intensity anomaly — and the stated conditioning mechanism will barely bind.

This is a cosmetic re-scaling of the archive's RND_CASH_VERIFIED_EXPENSE_WEDGE (identical second leg, R&D deflator swapped from sales to assets-plus-intangibles), and since Compustat intan already subsumes gdwl the MAX() is a no-op, leaving little substantive difference from an already-evaluated signal.

The depreciation add-back genuinely converts total accruals into a working-capital accrual proxy (ib−oancf+dp ≈ ΔWC), so the hypothesis and expression are consistent and the decomposition is a real economic refinement of the archive's goodwill-wedge result rather than a relabeling, though it remains a close cousin of GOODWILL_EARNINGS_CASH_WEDGE and inherits its weak Fama-MacBeth support.

With intan already including goodwill the MAX() is redundant, leaving a plain intangible-intensity × total-accruals product whose only change from already-tested archive variants is industry ranking — a cosmetic tweak on top of the standard accrual anomaly.

Multiplying signed revenue growth by a strictly positive R&D intensity makes the first leg non-monotone (declining-revenue, high-R&D firms are pushed to the bottom rank rather than the middle), and the receivables-absorption leg replicates the mechanism already tested and rejected in INTAN_DEMAND_WORKCAP_CASH_RELEASE plus the known receivables-accrual anomaly.

A coherent double-difference formulation whose sign logic matches the expression and which is structurally distinct from the level-based archive winner, though double-differencing is noisy and the second leg is close to the known change-in-accruals anomaly.
